entities.summary: Emile Percival Francis, nicknamed "The Cat", was a Canadian ice hockey player, coach, and general manager in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Chicago Black Hawks and New York Rangers from 1946 to 1952. After playing minor league hockey until 1960, he became the Rangers' assistant general manager in 1962 and later general manager of the Rangers, St. Louis Blues and Hartford Whalers from 1964 to 1989. Francis led the Rangers to nine consecutive playoff appearances (1967–75), but could not help deliver a Stanley Cup championship in five decades as a player, coach, and executive.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a general manager and coach in the NHL, Francis led the New York Rangers to nine consecutive playoff appearances from 1967 to 1975, demonstrating his impact on the team's success during this period. His tenure also saw significant changes in the league's management structure.
